tier_reason: First-party charts (docs/img/scorer.svg dated 2021-09-10, docs/img/cdist.svg dated 2022-10-02) generated by the public scripts bench/benchmark_scorer.py and bench/benchmark_cdist.py in rapidfuzz/RapidFuzz; every label in claimed_speedup matches the SVG text, but compiler, flags, CPU model, Python version and FuzzyWuzzy version are not stated, so the evidence falls short of A and stays C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Scorer called directly from Python, pairs per second RapidFuzz vs FuzzyWuzzy: ratio 6,206,379 vs 480,115 (12.9x), partial_ratio 3,091,339 vs 212,794 (14.5x), token_sort_ratio 3,155,091 vs 151,101 (20.9x), token_set_ratio 1,590,972 vs 108,940 (14.6x), partial_token_sort_ratio 1,767,978 vs 105,151 (16.8x), partial_token_set_ratio 1,213,823 vs 81,875 (14.8x), QRatio 5,231,998 vs 184,591 (28.3x), WRatio 1,264,866 vs 59,436 (21.3x). RapidFuzz through cdist vs FuzzyWuzzy in a Python double loop: ratio 135,463,598 vs 525,021 (258x), partial_ratio 12,936,872 vs 183,338 (71x), token_sort_ratio 120,274,547 vs 167,720 (717x), token_set_ratio 3,253,260 vs 117,282 (27.7x), partial_token_sort_ratio 4,610,742 vs 96,626 (47.7x), partial_token_set_ratio 2,090,213 vs 76,227 (27.4x), QRatio 126,989,691 vs 204,064 (622x), WRatio 2,516,289 vs 63,982 (39x). Ratios derived from page data (chart labels).
corrections.workload: Fuzzy string scorers (ratio, partial_ratio, token_sort_ratio, token_set_ratio, partial_token_sort_ratio, partial_token_set_ratio, QRatio, WRatio) over 10,000 random ASCII-letter-and-digit strings against 100 samples drawn from that list, reported as word pairs evaluated per second. Scorer chart (bench/benchmark_scorer.py): strings of length 10, both libraries called per pair from a Python list comprehension. cdist chart (bench/benchmark_cdist.py): strings of length 8, RapidFuzz timed as one process.cdist call (default workers=1, single-threaded) and FuzzyWuzzy timed as a Python double loop over inputs with the default processor applied before timing. Each measurement is a single timeit run (number=1).
corrections.caveats: The numbers measure the Python package rapidfuzz/RapidFuzz (which builds rapidfuzz-cpp from its extern/rapidfuzz-cpp submodule) against pure-Python-called FuzzyWuzzy, not C++ against a C++ baseline; nothing compares rapidfuzz-cpp itself with hand-written std::string code, and the seed's guessed std::string baseline does not apply. Harness: bench/benchmark_scorer.py and bench/benchmark_cdist.py in rapidfuzz/RapidFuzz (public), single timeit run per scorer, no compiler, flags, CPU, Python version or FuzzyWuzzy version stated, and it is not stated whether FuzzyWuzzy had the python-Levenshtein C speedup installed (without it FuzzyWuzzy falls back to difflib, which inflates the ratio). The cdist chart (2022-10-02) uses length-8 strings while the README text says length 10, and it compares a single batched C++ call (cdist with workers=1, so no threading, but with SIMD multi-string scorers) against per-pair Python calls, so its 258x to 717x figures mostly measure removed interpreter overhead plus batching rather than per-pair algorithmic gain. The scorer chart dates from 2021-09-10 and the numbers are old. RapidFuzz also deliberately fixes partial_ratio bugs, so results are not bit-identical to FuzzyWuzzy for that scorer. rapidfuzz-cpp's own bench/ directory (bench-fuzz.cpp, bench-levenshtein.cpp, bench-lcs.cpp, bench-jarowinkler.cpp, Google Benchmark) times RapidFuzz only against itself; the README's Benchmarks.md link returns 404 and the detailed comparison pages on rapidfuzz.github.io (Levenshtein vs editdistance, edlib, polyleven and others via bench/benchmark.py) are blocked here.

notes: Numbers on scorer.svg and cdist.svg match the record exactly (read from SVG text labels); metadata confirmed: MIT, 377 stars, 59 forks, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-08-30 ('update changelog'), Python package 4.2k stars. Shortcomings: Python-wrapper vs pure-Python-called FuzzyWuzzy baseline (not a C++ baseline), no hardware/compiler/flags, single-run timings, cdist chart compares batched C++ against a Python loop and uses length-8 strings, old charts (2021/2022). Enrichment lead: bench/benchmark.py in rapidfuzz/RapidFuzz compares Levenshtein, Indel, Jaro and DamerauLevenshtein against C/C++ libraries (editdistance, edlib, polyleven, jellyfish) whose plots live on the blocked docs site.
